extra.reason: Docs corrected: OPERATIONS.md gained a 'The reconnect budget' section naming the nats.go MaxReconnects(60) root cause and the two mechanisms that close it; the /ping and manual-restart claims are now historical or conditional; DATA_PLANE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md no longer claim the JetStream migration ended the failure mode; ADR 0003 amended rather than rewritten; CHANGELOG gained an Unreleased section. mkdocs build --strict passes.

Validated in-cluster on microk8s/thingsflow-fresh (helm rev 22, chart with the probe, image sha-f55a317). Baseline: all consumers restarts=0. Scaled statefulset thingsflow-nats to 0.

T+60s and T+120s: all 1/1 Running, restarts=0 -- the probe does NOT fire while the client can still reconnect, so no false positive on a survivable blip.
T+180s: the four Bento consumers went to restarts=1 while alarm-materializer stayed at 0. Kubernetes named the cause itself: 'Warning Unhealthy ... Liveness probe failed' events on nats-greptimedb, nats-latest-kv, nats-alarms and nats-entity-greptimedb, plus 'BackOff restarting failed container bento'. No Unhealthy event on any pod without the probe.
NATS restored: all five consumers returned to 1/1 Running on their own, and the consumer-guard reported thingsflow_nats_consumer_progress_ok 1, 'every consumer is bound and progressing' -- with no rollout restart by hand.

That is precisely what did not happen on 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-28, when the pods stayed Running 1/1 with their restart counts unchanged for hours.

Two limits worth recording. The guard took its 'caught up (backlog 0)' branch, not 'progressing', because nothing publishes on that cluster -- rebinding is proven, draining under load is not (production shows that daily). And the run was noisy: mid-test the cluster's own API server refused connections and DNS broke (nc: bad address). That is chronic there, not caused by the change -- coredns is on its 383rd restart, calico-kube-controllers its 383rd, metrics-server its 364th, all over ~386 days, on system pods unrelated to NATS. Lockstep restarts across every pod including probe-less ones came from that, not from any probe.

Test cluster torn down after the thingsflow-9ho verification, per the standing practice: deploy to verify a significant change, verify, shut down.

helm uninstall of the thingsflow release in thingsflow-fresh, then the three namespaces one at a time: tb-classic (empty, left from the fair benchmark), thingsflow (no release, only two Completed hook pods from 32 days ago and three PVCs nothing claimed) and thingsflow-fresh (the stack the probe was validated on).

All six ThingsFlow PVs released and reclaimed automatically -- microk8s-hostpath is reclaim policy Delete. hostpath storage went from 4.5G to 3.7G and the node disk from 62% to 53%; the remaining PV is the in-cluster registry's. Only ingress-nginx and tailscale-operator helm releases are left, which is the cluster's baseline.

Noted but not touched, because it is neither ours nor new: a Failed PV 'source-pv' claimed by bacnet-explorer/source-pvc, a namespace that no longer exists, 384 days old.

Applied to production as helm rev 64 (2026-09-15 15:43Z): alarms.energy voltageLowV 110, voltageHighV 125, voltageClearLowV 112, voltageClearHighV 123 (CSA C235 normal band for 120 V), live values captured to a file, never --reuse-values.

Diff proven before applying with --dry-run=server: exactly the four ALARM_VOLTAGE_* env values on thingsflow-nats-alarms, nothing else. A plain --dry-run showed a spurious checksum/device-jwt-key change to sha256('') -- a client-side render artifact of the chart's Secret lookup, because the helm snap had silently moved to v4.3.0, where --dry-run defaults to client. Applied with --server-side=false to keep rev 63's apply method explicitly rather than trusting Helm 4's 'auto'.

Outcome in production: only the nats-alarms pod rolled; rmqtt-edge, flow-core and the materializer untouched. Post-upgrade hooks nats-bootstrap and greptimedb-retention Complete, no warning events. The materializer logged 'cleared' for 19 of 19 VoltageOutOfRange types by 15:43:53, then only 'noop' -- 114 noops across 6 cycles, zero extended or created. Consumer and freshness guards green after the rollout.

The third acceptance criterion was verified without injecting fake readings into production (that would raise a real alarm for a real device and write a false sample to GreptimeDB): the real bento-nats-alarms pipeline, run locally on Bento 1.8.1 with stdin/stdout, gave create_or_update for 116.8 V under the old 207/253 band (the bug reproduced), and under the new band clear for 116.8 V and create_or_update for both 130 V and 100 V.

Not versioned anywhere: no production values file exists in the repo, only *.example.yaml templates, so the override lives in the release's stored values and survives only while upgrades start from helm get values.
